# Explicit majorants for the native reconstruction precision

2026-11-12. Parent derivation under focused review. This supplies computable
majorants for the already proved height chain; it is not an implementation
of Arakelov geometry, a semistable-model algorithm, or a new surface theorem.
Do not use the particular numerical constants below until checked. The prior
effective-polynomial proof and its hypotheses remain in the linked reviews.

## Input and aim

On ONE geometrically connected component let d be its cover degree, g its
genus, r>=3 a bound on the total branch orbit, and hB a computed upper bound
on absolute LOGARITHMIC branch heights. The native plane model has known
degree and rational coefficient bit bounds. Choose the common integer a>0,
regular at the auxiliary prime, and the residue-good coordinate c as in the
reconstruction review. Their actual integer values are known. All formula
evaluation can use outward rational/integer bounds on logarithms.

Aim: produce an integer K bounding every rational product/interpolation
coefficient's logarithmic height, so P^e>2*exp(2K) certifies reconstruction.
No unknown torsion field or analytic chart is constructed. Field extensions
in the height proof occur only inside normalized inequalities.

## An explicit analytic constant

Use the exact angular Whitney/root atlas in merkl-log-atlas. Write
L=1+log(1/delta), theta0=(delta/100)(3/4)^d, a(s)=min(1/4,dist(s,B)),
rho(s)=a(s)/100. Its balls of radius rho(s)/16 are disjoint. For a dyadic
layer t<=a(s)<2t, each ball has spherical area at least t^2/1600^2 and
their union is inside r caps of radius3t and total area at most36r t^2.
Hence there are fewer than2^27*r centers per layer. The capped layer has
fewer than2^29 centers, by the total sphere area and radius1/6400. There
are at most2L+d+10 layers. Including every lift and the at-most-rd branch
charts, the deliberately loose bound

    N <= 2^42(r+1)d(d+L)

suffices. The already proved full-chart density and ordered-overlap bounds
are c1<=d^2 and M<=500d(4/3)^d, so log M<=9d. Actual Javanpeykar/Bruin
Theorem3.1.2 at inner radius7/8 bounds BOTH the Green upper bound and its
local two-sided regularization by2^16*N*d^2. This also bounds the3/4 version.

The exact product formula gives average L<=L0, where

    L0=1+r(r-1)(2hB+1),
    Lambda=2^60(r+1)d^3(d+L0).

Thus Lambda bounds the relevant embedding-averaged analytic quantities.
No exponential in hB, uncomputed real separation, optimized decimal
constant, spectral estimate, or ineffective existence theorem occurs.

## Point, Faltings, theta and discriminant majorants

For a positive integer v define

    Z(v)=Lambda+(d+1)r(hB+log(1+v)+1)+2d^2 log d+7.

The actual finite div(d pi) intersection identity, not just contraction to
the minimal model, bounds h_Z(b)<=Z(v) on the SPECIFIC cover-compatible
semistable normalization-resolution for pi(b)=v. It combines source
Proposition4.2.4/Theorem4.3.2 with the point-height proof's differential
bound1/800. The finite extension degree cancels after normalization.
It is invalid to replace this Z by an arbitrary additional blowup model.

Set v0=g^3+r+1, A_g=g(g+1)/2 and

    W=A_g*Lambda+[g(g-1)/2]log4+(g/2)log(2g^2 d^2),
    F=A_g*Z(v0)+W,
    Delta=2g(g+1)(4g+1)*Z(v0)+12W+93g^3,
    Theta=(g/4)log max(1,F)+(4g^3+5g+1)log2.

Some v<=v0 has no Weierstrass point above it. Actual source Theorem2.4.1
and Lemma2.4.2 therefore bound h_Fal by F, minimal semistable node sum by
Delta, and averaged log theta supremum by Theta. No test for that auxiliary
height-proof point is needed by the algorithm: monotonic Z(v0) is a bound
for an existing suitable v. This is distinct from the ACTUAL common a
whose height enters the canonical divisor calculation next.

## Canonical support majorant from the proved intersection chain

For the actual a put Z=Z(a), and take a generous spherical derivative
constant1000d in the global Green lower bound. Define

    Ccross=Z+Lambda+log(1000d)+(1/2)log(1+a^2),
    Hpi=d*Lambda+(1/2)log(1+a^2)
                    +d[log(1000d)+Lambda+1/2],
    Vpi=d*(Z+Delta),
    Support=d*[A_g*Z+2g^2*Delta+Theta+(g/2)log(2pi)+F/2+g*Ccross]
                    +g*[d*Lambda+Hpi+Vpi].

Then the finite/analytic chain in SURFACE_TORSION_HEIGHT_CHAIN.md bounds
sum_(Q in D_t with multiplicity) h(pi(Q)) by Support. The formula deliberately
overcounts the nonnegative cross/contraction terms. It retains the book's
actual -[D.(D-omega)]/2 sign, TWO distinct pole/Green contributions, and
log(2pi). It applies to torsion classes and unique canonical D_t with all
specified support exclusions. It does not claim a height bound for arbitrary
representatives or for a basepoint whose height was omitted.

All quantities are polynomials with fixed exponents in d,g,hB,log(1+a).
For fixed r and g=O_r(d) this is the effective version of the loose d^9*S
support envelope. A simpler larger power bound can be used, but is unnecessary.

## Closed coordinates without an unnamed jet constant

Let Fplane(x,y) be the known GLOBAL rational monic plane equation restricted
to a component, of total degree D. Fix an integral representative of its
coefficient vector and compute upper bounds on its affine coefficient
height and number of monomials. Root-height/specialization gives a computable
bound H on the sum of multiplicity-weighted h(x)+h(y) from Support and those
coefficients. It is enough to use this same H as an upper bound on EVERY
individual support point's coordinate-height sum; this weakens the bound
only polynomially. The actual model coefficients, not intrinsic theta data,
pay the coordinate change.

For eta=F_y-c F_x and V=F_y partial_x-F_x partial_y, compute the polynomial
recurrences separately for f=x,y:

    P_1=F_y or -F_x,
    P_(n+1)=eta V(P_n)-(2n-1)P_n V(eta), 1<=n<g.

They have degree<=2nD and polynomial coefficient bit size (each step adds
two fixed F/eta factors, not a square of the previous P_n). The polynomials
have only two variables, so constructing this formal recurrence is itself
polynomial. Their exact coefficient bit lengths give explicit majorants
B_n, with no unknown constant. For a polynomial P of degree e and M terms,
use h(P(Q))<=h_aff(P)+eH+log max(1,M). Denote this bound by Eval(P).

Each normalized Taylor coefficient is bounded by

    Jet_n=Eval(P_n)+(2n-1)Eval(eta)+log(n!), n>=1;
    Jet_0=H.

If P_n is identically zero its contribution is zero. Nonzero eta values are
guaranteed by the already checked residue condition; h(eta^-1)=h(eta) pays
all small denominators. A coarse joint jet bound is
J=2g^2*max_(f=x,y,0<=n<g) Jet_n.

Use Hz=g[H+log(1+|c|)+log2]. Confluent interpolation then gives the explicit
closed-encoding majorant

    Hclosed=(Hz+g log2)+(g Hz+g^2 log2+J+log(g!)).

The first term bounds A; the second bounds the shared-denominator vector
of B,C via Cramer's rule. These are intrinsic absolute heights: a splitting
field may be used in the proof but its degree does not multiply the bound.
Nonsplit and nonreduced divisors are included. A coordinate denominator from
the monic transformation is treated by the same known polynomial evaluation
and inverse-height rules after its residue unit check.

## Rational reconstruction threshold

Add the explicit fibre-point height bound and height-zero cyclotomic entry
to bound every scalar in the all-pair encoding by Henc. Let N_S=|Gamma|ell^m,
q be its known tuple length and u the chosen integer separator. Put

    Halpha=q Henc+q^2 log(u+2)+log(q+1),
    Hlambda=3(N_S-1)Halpha+2(N_S-1)log2,
    K=N_S^2*(Halpha+2Hlambda)+2log N_S+N_S*(Halpha+log2)+1.

This dominates the product polynomial, fixed-arity operation and Boolean
relation coefficients from the explicit Lagrange formulas. Global equivariance
proves they are rational; auxiliary separation proves their denominators are
P-units. Take an integer T>=exp(K) by outward bit rounding and choose e with
P^e>2T^2. These known bounds pay every precision digit. Semistable models,
complex atlas evaluation and global torsion splitting fields are not inputs.

# Uniform arithmetic height: established pieces and remaining coordinate bound

2026-11-12. Native classical surface comparison remains OPEN. This note
records proved sub-obligations from the accelerated closure round.
Paid reports remain advisory; independent proofs and actual sources were
parent-checked. No whole point-counting, novelty or quantum-separation claim.

## Stable Faltings height is now bounded uniformly

Fix r>=3. For every finite degree-d map pi:Y->P1 over Qbar with Y smooth,
projective, connected of genus g>=1 and total Galois orbit of branch points
of cardinality <=r, put hB=max h(beta), ABSOLUTE LOGARITHMIC projective height.
Then, for an effective C_r depending only on r,

    h_Fal(Y) <= C_r*d^5*(d+1+hB).

Proof and exact source ledger:
audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-faltings-transfer.md. It combines the proved
MERKL_LOG_COLLISION_ATLAS.md with actual Javanpeykar1403.6404 Theorem2.4.1,
Lemma2.3.1, Proposition4.2.4 and Theorem4.3.2. It does not reinterpret the
source's exponential HB as logarithmic. Field enlargement in the height
proof is existential and cancels after normalization; no algorithm for a
semistable model or its extension field is asserted.

The precise product-formula identity is
I_fin(P,Q)+sum_sigma log(1/vartheta_sigma(P,Q))=[K:Q](h(P)+h(Q)),
with vartheta using maximum homogeneous norms. Consequently both normalized
finite intersections and average log inverse chordal distance are bounded
by h(P)+h(Q)+log2. Thus average L_sigma<=1+r(r-1)(2hB+log2).

The FULL Merkl atlas gives |log||dz||_Ar|<=Lambda_sigma, not just sup gr.
The actual angular Whitney/root charts also have
|d(pi^*t)/dz|>=dist_ch(pi(x),B)/800 at finite base values. For a rational
a outside B, every b over a therefore satisfies

    hAr(b) <= Lambda_bar +(d+1)*sum_beta(h(beta)+h(a)+log2)
              +2d²logd+log800,
    Lambda_bar <= C_r*d³*(d+1+hB).

The finite term uses the general-cover normalization with vertical branch
only at primes<=d; horizontal branch collisions are explicitly charged by
the same product formula. The factorial-normalized source Wronskian has
lognorm<=g(g+1)Lambda_sigma/2+O(g²+glog(gd)) by Cauchy/Hadamard and
full-chart density<=d². Choose a among1,...,g³+r+1 avoiding branch and
Weierstrass images; g=O_r(d) and h(a)=O_r(logd). Actual Theorem2.4.1 gives
the displayed h_Fal bound, including genus one and branches at infinity.

This proves an intrinsic inequality, not model-coordinate heights or
reconstruction precision. The twist family y²=a*x(x-1)(x-2) still forces
charging supplied-model coefficients. The completed Claude faltings report
is accepted after repairing its containing-branch-set equality and Wronskian
normalization. No theorem is inferred from its verdict label.

## Averaged theta and stable discriminant budgets

Source-checked review: audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-theta-delta.md.
The book4.4.5, Javanpeykar and Wilms use the SAME determinant-normalized
theta norm. Javanpeykar Lemma2.4.2 states exactly

    Theta_av <= (g/4)log max(1,h_Fal)+(4g³+5g+1)log2,

where Theta_av is the embedding AVERAGE of log sup norms, not a pointwise
embedding bound. Put S=d+1+hB. The established Faltings bound gives
Theta_av<=C_r[d³+d log S]. This directly pays the book9.2.5 theta term.
No exponentially sized theta embedding is constructed or needed.

The same existing small non-Weierstrass point and factorial-normalized
Wronskian budget, substituted in actual Javanpeykar Theorem2.4.1, give

    Delta_st <= C_r*d^6*S,       delta_Fal <= C_r*d^5*S.

Delta_st is the normalized node sum on the RELATIVELY MINIMAL regular
semistable model. It does not bound node sums after arbitrary blowups.
No effective semistable extension/model algorithm follows. The independent
Wilms check gives log thetaSup<=log c_g+delta/24+(g/3)log(2pi), with
log c_g=O(g log(g+2)); averaging also works but is unnecessary here.

New proposed transfer from these budgets to actual torsion support heights
is in SURFACE_TORSION_HEIGHT_CHAIN.md, explicitly UNDER REVIEW. These source

## One common point makes canonical divisors unique

For ANY smooth projective geometrically connected genus-g curve C/k and ANY
N geometric degree-zero classes T, assume char0 or char(k)>2g-2. Outside at
most

    [0 in T]*(g³-g)+|T\{0}|*floor(g(g-1)²/2) <= N*g³

geometric points b, every E in T has h0(E(gb))=1. Hence it has a UNIQUE
effective degree-g representative D_E. This descends as a CLOSED divisor
over the field fixing b and E, without splitting geometric supports.

Independent proof: audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-common-basepoint.md.
RR reduces failure to a section of K tensor E^-1 vanishing to order g.
The complete-series Wronskian has local leading Vandermonde in vanishing

Characteristic is a real gate: the smooth char3 plane quartic

For a separable plane map of degree D with discriminant exclusions R,

field of degree<=D. Test h0=1 for every supplied class by charged RR. For
rank m fixed, enumeration of ell^m classes is polynomial. Every class is
already represented over the native module's ONE common field; do not
take a growing arbitrary lcm of support fields. RR costs charge positive
and negative divisor degrees and presentations. Randomized subroutines
need capped independent restarts, not an assumed tail from expectation.

Original Frobenius/deck maps need the basepoint correction:

    D_(sigma E)^b is the unique effective member of
        |sigma(D_E^b)+g*b-g*sigma(b)|.

Replacing original Frobenius by an extension power is invalid. In char0,
a base value of height<=log(Ng³+R+1) exists; coordinate/Arakelov comparison
must still be paid. Under an ACTUAL smooth DVR model, section b and extended
line bundle E, h0=1 on the special fibre gives H1=0 and a free rank-one H0;
the canonical divisor is finite flat and specializes correctly. This is
compatibility, not an algorithm constructing those extensions.

## Exact remaining height obligation

The completed OpenAI torsion-height report correctly separates chosen small
b from arbitrary b: uniqueness alone cannot omit its height. On the fixed
elliptic curve y²=x³-2x, P=(2,2), Q=(0,0), b_N=[2^N]P gives
v2 x(b_N)=-2N and v2 x(b_N+Q)=2N+1. Unique degree-one representatives of
the fixed nonzero2-torsion class have unbounded coefficient heights. This
illustrates the missing basepoint charge; ell2 is not an odd-ell surface
counterfamily. The zero class D_0=g*b already forces the same charge at
every ell. This does NOT refute a controlled choice of small b.

Source TheoremB.4's constants are not polynomial in growing g: its displayed
comparison has4^g factors and its Jacobian representation can have exponential

classes and unique divisors give polynomial individual support degrees, not

The current decisive obligation is polynomial height of CLOSED torsion-divisor
encodings for a controlled b, with model height charged. An explicit source

Their vertical terms, support-closure hypotheses, cross-intersections and

# Canonical torsion-divisor support heights

2026-11-12. Parent derivation independently checked in
audits/reviews/2026-11-12-torsion-height-{finite,analytic}-chain.md; both full
reviews were parent-read. The completed OpenAI contraction report independently
obtained the graph bound. This proves the scoped support-VALUE height theorem
below, not a closed encoding or native surface algorithm. The direct broad
paid book-height request was empty. Retain the book signs and minimality guard.

## Input and proved bound

Let pi:C->P1 be a degree-d cover over Qbar, smooth connected C of genus
g>=1, with fixed total branch orbit <=r and logarithmic branch height hB.
Let T be N degree-zero torsion classes. Choose b over a SMALL NONZERO
INTEGER a outside branch/exceptional values such that every D_t in |t+gb|
is unique and avoids the poles of pi. All divisors are closed; field
extensions below are existential for normalized height bounds, not a
common splitting-field algorithm. Set S_N=d+1+hB+log(N+1). If A additional
geometric points must be avoided, replace log(N+1) by log(N(A+1)+1).

The lemmas below establish:

    sum_(Q with multiplicity in D_t) h(pi(Q)) <= C_r*d^9*S_N.

The exponent is deliberately loose. A supplied plane-model coordinate y
can then be charged using its equation F(pi,y)=0 and its coefficient
height H: h(y(Q))<=poly(deg F)*(H+h(pi(Q))+1), away from the finitely many
places requiring a different affine/normalization chart. Avoiding those
places is a separate finite bad-basepoint condition. A full closed-divisor
encoding still needs a precise primitive-coordinate/jet reconstruction
argument; a polynomial for pi-values alone can lose branch labels.

## Finite model-transfer lemma

Let Z be the regular semistable cover-compatible model from the reviewed
Javanpeykar construction, with pi a MORPHISM to P1 over the integers.
Let f:Z->Y contract to the relatively minimal regular semistable model.
Work after finite extension so horizontal supports and components split.
Every contraction is a rational (-1) tail, inverse to blowing up a smooth
point; blowing up a node would introduce a multiplicity-two component.

For a section b define L_s(b) as the number of smooth blowup centres traversed
by its successive images. Each contributes one. Then

    sum_s L_s(b) log Norm(s) / [K:Q]
       = h_Z(b)-h_Y(b) <= h_Z(b),

by omega_Z=f^*omega_Y+exceptional contributions, identical archimedean
metrics, and nonnegativity of stable Arakelov point height. For every
distinct section P,

    I_Y,s(b,P) <= I_Z,s(b,P)+L_s(b).

Each smooth-point blowup changes the intersection of two sections by one
exactly when both pass through the centre. Consequently, for the degree-d
horizontal zero/pole divisors Z0,Pinf of pi,

    I_Y,s(b,Pinf) <= d L_s(b),
    I_Y,s(b,Z0) <= v_s(a)+d L_s(b).

The first uses that integral a and infinity sections are disjoint on the
base and pi is a morphism on Z. The second uses restriction of div(pi)
near b on Z: it is effective there, so its horizontal zero intersection
is <=v_s(a). This explicitly charges collisions with zero at primes |a.

## Vertical-pole bound on the minimal model

Write div_Y(pi)=Z0-Pinf+sum_C v_C C in a fibre at s. The dual graph is
connected, with unit edges and delta_s geometric nodes; loops are harmless.
Intersecting a principal divisor with components makes v solve the graph
Laplacian equation with current vector from Z0-Pinf. Its total positive
current is <=d. Therefore

    max_C v_C-min_C v_C <= d delta_s.

Proof: choose a threshold between the endpoint values of any
edge. All crossing currents have the same sign, so that edge's voltage
drop is at most the total positive source d. Connect extrema by a path
with <=delta_s edges. No inverse spectral-gap estimate is used.

A section meets a smooth point of a regular semistable fibre. Restriction
of div(pi) to b gives

    v_Cb = v_s(a)-I_Y,s(b,Z0)+I_Y,s(b,Pinf) >= -d L_s(b).

Hence m_s(pi)=max(0,-min_C v_C) <=d(L_s(b)+delta_s), and

    V_pi := sum_s m_s(pi)log Norm(s)/[K:Q]
        <= d[h_Z(b)+Delta_st(C)].

Equivalently use u=pi-(a-1), so u(b)=1. Its zeros and b are disjoint on Z,
its poles and negative vertical valuations agree with pi, and the same
graph proof gives the bound without a v_s(a) term. This pays the vertical
term using stable discriminant, without bounding the nonminimal node count.
Z must be the SPECIFIC source normalization-resolution: its finite
div(d pi) identity bounds h_Z(b), not merely h_Y(b). An arbitrary further
blowup is not free. Splitting fields here prove heights only; node subdivision
under base change preserves normalized Delta and crepant canonical heights.

## Removal of book9.1.3's support-etale assumption

On a regular semistable model and a section Q outside the generic zero and
pole supports, restriction of the principal divisor gives

    max(0,-v_s(pi(Q))) <= I_s(Q,Pinf)+m_s(pi).

When pi(Q)=0, its finite coordinate-height contribution is zero and the
inequality holds directly; do not restrict the zero principal function.
Thus collisions between horizontal zero and pole sections do not by
themselves obstruct the finite inequality. At an archimedean place let
G=gr with log-distance singularity, and put

    u(Q)=0.5 log(1+|pi(Q)|²)+G(Pinf,Q),
    H_pi=0.5 integral_C log(1+|pi|²) mu.

The Green representation for dd^c u=pi^*FS-d mu is

    u(Q)=integral_C G(Q,R) pi^*FS(R)+H_pi.

It gives u(Q)<=d sup G+H_pi. Summing the local inequalities is precisely
the book coordinate-height inequality, without demanding disjoint
horizontal supports. The actual source's final identity has this plus sign;
its opposite Laplacian convention does not change the final formula.

## Archimedean moment bound

Use the SAME b above a. The established global lower bound is

    G(b,R)>=log dist_ch(a,pi(R))-log(Cd)-Lambda',

away from equal base images, which form a measure-zero set. Since pi has
degree d and FS has total mass one,

    integral_C log dist_ch(a,pi(R)) pi^*FS(R)=-d/2.

Evaluate the Green identity at b, and use G(Pinf,b)<=d sup G:

    H_pi <= d sup G+0.5 log(1+a²)
              +d[log(Cd)+Lambda'+1/2].

All embedding averages are polynomial in d,hB,log(N+1) by the existing
Merkl bound and the small integer choice of a. No charts need to be
constructed algorithmically for this height inequality.

## Assembly with actual book9.2.5

On Y take D=g b. Arakelov adjunction gives b²=-h_Y(b)[K:Q], hence
-(D,D-omega)/2 = g(g+1)h_Y(b)[K:Q]/2. Dropping the nonnegative
log-cardinality term, the source bounds each (D_t,P) by this term plus
2g² Delta_st, the theta-supremum sum, g log(2pi)/2, half the Faltings
height, and (g b,P). For P over infinity the finite cross-intersection
is <=h_Z(b), and the established global Green lower bound pays its
archimedean part by Lambda'+log(Cd)+0.5 log(1+a²).

Sum this over Pinf with multiplicities (total degree d). Then sum the
coordinate-height inequality over the degree-g divisor D_t itself:

    sum_Q h(pi(Q)) <= (D_t,Pinf)/[K:Q]
                      +g[d sup G_bar+H_pi_bar+V_pi].

Known bounds h_Z(b)<=C_r d³ S_N, Delta_st<=C_r d^6(d+1+hB),
Theta_av<=C_r[d³+d log(d+1+hB)], h_Fal<=C_r d^5(d+1+hB) give the
d^9 S_N envelope. This is not yet a certified reconstruction
algorithm and does not address native frame/good-model constructions.

## Finite support avoidance

For any specified forbidden point P and any class t, D_t contains P iff
H0(K_C tensor t^-1 tensor O(P)) has a section vanishing to order >=g at b.
That space has dimension g and degree 2g-1. Its ordinary Wronskian is
nonzero in characteristic zero (or characteristic>2g-1) and has degree
g(2g-1)+g(g-1)²=g³. Thus at most Ng³ times the number of forbidden
geometric points must be added to the common-basepoint bad set. This
pays avoidance of poles and plane-chart exceptions with small log-height
base values; it must not be invoked in unrestricted characteristic.

The combined bad-basepoint count is at most Ng³(1+d+A), plus r branch
values. Choosing an integer a<=r+Ng³(1+d+A)+1 outside their images ensures
EVERY b above a works; its logarithmic height has the advertised bound.

Status: transfer, graph, moment, assembly and avoidance claims are independently
checked and parent-accepted in the stated scope. Existing input theorems and their
precise sources are in SURFACE_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_HEIGHT.md and reviews
surface-theta-delta, merkl-log-atlas, surface-faltings-transfer and book-height-
minimality. Closed divisor encoding, faithful input presentation, and rational
reconstruction remain separate interfaces. No full comparator, speedup or

For projective points, use

```
h((x0:x1)) = (1/D_K) sum_v log max(|x0|_v,|x1|_v).
```

sections in `P1_O_K`, including the logarithms of residue norms. Define

```

 = |sigma(Delta)| /
   [max(|sigma x0|,|sigma x1|) max(|sigma y0|,|sigma y1|)].
```

Primitive local homogeneous coordinates give

```
I_v(P,Q) = [ord_v(Delta)-min_i ord_v(x_i)-min_i ord_v(y_i)] log #k(v).

```

  = D_K*(h(P)+h(Q)).                                      (1)
```

```

(1/D_K) sum_sigma log(1/dist_ch(sigma P,sigma Q))
  <= h(P)+h(Q)+log 2.                                     (3)

# Closed divisor encoding from support heights

2026-11-12. Independent exact review following
`SURFACE_TORSION_HEIGHT_CHAIN.md` and the completed finite/analytic reviews.
Those reviews supply support-height premises; their geometric/model inputs
are not re-proved here. No Git, network, API, archive, or numerical test was
used.

**Disposition.** There is a polynomial-height rational univariate encoding
of the requested nonreduced divisor. A separating coordinate must also be
unramified at every support point. Derivative denominators and the
confluent interpolation determinant both admit polynomial logarithmic
height bounds. Construction from a closed divisor algebra uses exact
linear algebra, without splitting the support. A numerical bit bound
additionally charges the presentation height of the field of definition,
not only its degree. This is not a construction of that field, a lift, a
good model, or the divisor from its abstract class alone.

## 1. Precise contract and output

Work in characteristic zero. Let K be an explicitly presented number
field over which the plane curve and the effective divisor E are defined.
Take a reduced plane equation F of total degree D; the application has an
absolutely irreducible curve. Its smooth normalization is C. Assume every
point of E maps into the affine nonsingular locus of the plane curve.
There the normalization is an isomorphism. Write geometrically

    E = sum_i m_i P_i,    P_i=(alpha_i,beta_i),
    sum_i m_i=g >= 1,    P_i distinct.

Let h denote absolute logarithmic Weil height. Use the projective
coefficient height H_F of F, and suppose

    sum_i m_i (h(alpha_i)+h(beta_i)) <= H.                 (1)

If the given support-height budget counts distinct points without
multiplicity, g times that budget suffices for (1). All geometric
conjugate points in the divisor are counted. Coefficients of F may be
normalized by one nonzero coefficient; the resulting affine coefficient
vector has height H_F. No bound below depends on its scalar normalization.

For a suitable integer c, put z=x+c y and h_c=log max(1,|c|). There exist

    A(T) monic, deg A=g;     B(T), C(T), deg B,deg C<g,

over K such that K[E] is K[T]/(A), with x=B(T), y=C(T), and z=T.
One absolute constant C_0 gives the joint coefficient-height bound

    h([1, coeff(A), coeff(B), coeff(C)])
       <= C_0 { D g H + g^2[H_F+h_c+log(gD+2)] }.          (2)

This is an intrinsic coefficient-height statement, valid without taking
the support's splitting field as an output field. Section 6 states the
extra field-presentation data needed to turn (2) into a bit bound.

The field must fix E as an effective divisor, not merely its linear
equivalence class. In the canonical application, uniqueness of the
effective representative supplies this distinction: a field fixing the
curve, basepoint, and class also fixes that unique divisor.

## 2. One small coordinate for N divisors

Set

    eta = F_y-c F_x.

On the smooth curve, z is a local parameter precisely when eta(P) is
nonzero. Indeed V=F_y partial_x-F_x partial_y is a nonzero tangent vector
there and V(z)=eta. At a fixed smooth point there is at most one bad c;
if F_x(P)=0, there is none. For two distinct affine plane points there is
at most one c with alpha_i+c beta_i=alpha_j+c beta_j. If beta_i=beta_j,
there is none. Thus a divisor of degree g excludes at most

    binom(s,2)+s <= g(g+1)/2

values, where s is its number of distinct support points. For N divisors,
the integer grid

    {0,1,...,N g(g+1)/2}

contains a c good for all of them, with h_c<=log(1+Ng^2). Divisors of
degrees at most g obey the same bound. Separation is required within
each divisor, not between different divisors. The search cost is
polynomial in N and the presented divisor data; only the height cost is
logarithmic in N. No claim of enumeration time polynomial in log N is
made.

This is where the smooth-plane-support premise matters: two distinct
normalization branches over the same singular plane point cannot be
separated by any function x+c y. The excluded points are counted in
Section 7.

## 3. Exact scheme encoding and descent

Put z_i=alpha_i+c beta_i. Since eta(P_i) is nonzero,
t_i=z-z_i is a uniformizer. Over an algebraic closure,

    Kbar[E] = product_i Kbar[t_i]/(t_i^m_i).

The z_i are distinct, so the Chinese remainder theorem gives

    A(T)=product_i (T-z_i)^m_i,
    Kbar[T]/(A) ~= Kbar[E].                               (3)

There are unique polynomials B,C of degree less than g that match the
Taylor expansions of x,y in t_i through order m_i-1. In particular,

    B+c C = T mod A,
    F(B,C)=0 mod A,
    eta(B,C) is a unit mod A.                             (4)

Equations (3)--(4) and uniqueness are Galois invariant. Consequently
A,B,C belong to K. The affine ideal of the divisor is

    ( A(x+c y), x-B(x+c y), y-C(x+c y) ).                 (5)

Its quotient is K[T]/(A), and F lies in the ideal by (4). On the smooth
curve, its local ideal at P_i is (t_i^m_i), as required. This is the
divisor thickening on the curve, not the m_i-th power of a plane maximal
ideal. Repeated roots of A are intentional and preserve multiplicities.

## 4. Jets: denominator and numerator bounds

The derivative along z on the function field is

    D_z = V/eta,    V=F_y partial_x-F_x partial_y.

For f=x or y, induction gives, for n>=1,

    D_z^n f = P_n/eta^(2n-1),
    P_1=F_y or -F_x,
    P_(n+1)=eta V(P_n)-(2n-1)P_n V(eta).                 (6)

For D>=2,

    deg P_n <= D-1+(n-1)(2D-3) <= 2nD.                  (7)

For D=1 the derivatives of order at least two vanish, so the coarse
bound still holds. At every nonarchimedean place use the coefficient
Gauss norm; at every archimedean place use the coefficient l1 norm.
Multiplication is submultiplicative, differentiation increases the norm
by at most the degree, and the sum in (6) introduces only its two terms.
Each step adds two factors from F/eta and a logarithm O(log(nD+2)); it
does not double the preceding numerator height. After the normalization
of F in Section 1, this proves

    h_aff(coeff P_n) <= C n[H_F+h_c+log(nD+2)].           (8)

The l1-to-coefficient-max conversion contributes O(log(D+2)) per fixed
F factor and is included in (8). Write
h_i=h(alpha_i)+h(beta_i). Polynomial evaluation gives

    h(eta(P_i)) <= H_F+h_c+D h_i+C log(D+2),
    h(P_n(P_i)) <= C n[H_F+h_c+D h_i+log(nD+2)].          (9)

The normalized Taylor coefficient is

    j_(i,n)(f)=P_n(P_i)/(n! eta(P_i)^(2n-1)).

Since h(a^-1)=h(a) for a nonzero algebraic number, and
log(n!)<=n log n, (9) proves

    h(j_(i,n)(f)) <= C n[H_F+h_c+D h_i+log(nD+2)]         (10)

for n>=1; the n=0 coefficient is alpha_i or beta_i. Thus small derivative
denominators and large multiplicities are explicitly paid. In particular
there is no factorial-sized logarithmic precision demand hidden in the
Taylor expansion.

Summing the jet heights for both x and y and n<m_i yields

    J <= C {D g H + g^2[H_F+h_c+log(gD+2)]},             (11)

using sum_i m_i^2<=g^2 and sum_i m_i^2 h_i<=gH.

## 5. Confluent interpolation: no uncharged root separation

In the Taylor normalization above, the interpolation matrix is

    W_((i,n),j)=binom(j,n) z_i^(j-n),
    0<=n<m_i,  0<=j<g,

with entries zero when j<n. Its determinant is, up to the sign of the
row order,

    det W=product_(i<j)(z_j-z_i)^(m_i m_j) != 0.         (12)

There are no extra factorial factors. Put

    H_z=sum_i m_i h(z_i) <= H+g(h_c+log 2).

The height of A's coefficient vector is at most H_z+g log 2. The affine
height of a row of W is at most (g-1)h(z_i)+g log 2. Hence the sum of
these row heights is at most gH_z+g^2 log 2.

Apply Cramer's rule to the two jet right-hand sides. At each place bound
all relevant determinants by the product of the maxima of their rows;
at archimedean places the permutation sum costs log(g!), not g! times
the row-height bound. Use rows enlarged by the two jet entries, so the
same bound covers det W and every numerator determinant simultaneously.
The homogeneous vector

    [det W, all B-numerators, all C-numerators]

therefore has height at most gH_z+g^2 log 2+J+log(g!). It represents
[1,coeff B,coeff C]; the product formula pays the common denominator.
Combining this with A's bound and (11) proves (2).

Although a splitting field can be used for this proof, its degree never
multiplies (2). The auxiliary conjugate computations are normalized
absolute-height inequalities. For a conditioning check, if e=[K:Q], each
support point has degree at most eg over Q, while a pair lies in a field
of degree at most eg^2. Thus the nonzero values eta(P_i) and z_i-z_j have
polynomial logarithmic lower bounds at each embedding by
log|sigma(a)|>=-[Q(a):Q]h(a). No factorial splitting-field degree or
independent separation promise is needed. These lower bounds do not
amount to an algorithm that labels or computes the individual roots.

## 6. Closed-algebra construction and actual bit scope

Suppose E is supplied by its finite K-algebra R=H^0(E,O_E), with unit and
multiplication by x and y, or by a closed ideal from which this algebra
is computed with the input representation cost charged. For a candidate
integer c form M_z=M_x+c M_y. Both goodness conditions have tests over K:

* F_y(M_x,M_y)-cF_x(M_x,M_y) is invertible;
* the columns 1,z,...,z^(g-1) form a basis of R.

The first tests eta on the reduced support. The second tests that z
generates the entire, possibly nonreduced, algebra. At a good c both
hold. Take A=charpoly(M_z); solve the power-basis linear systems for the
coordinates B of x and C of y. Cyclicity makes this characteristic
polynomial the degree-g minimal polynomial, giving precisely (3)--(5).
This needs polynomially many field operations and standard exact linear
algebra. It neither factors A nor constructs the joint support splitting
field. For multiple divisors, the tests can be done separately over their
own charged definition fields with the same integer c.

Let e=[K:Q], and charge a concrete field presentation of height B_K,
including any basis changes. For example K=Q(theta) in its power basis
has h(theta) bounded by the height of its supplied defining polynomial.
The trace Gram matrix

    T_ij=Tr_(K/Q)(theta^(i+j)),    0<=i,j<e,

has entries of height polynomial in e and B_K; its determinant is
nonzero by separability. Cramer's rule gives a trace-dual basis beta_j
of height polynomial in e and B_K, with no lower-discriminant assumption.
If a=sum_j q_j theta^j, then q_j=Tr(a beta_j), so

    h(q_j) <= e h(a)+poly(e,B_K).                        (13)

Using (2) in (13), every rational coordinate of A,B,C has numerator and
denominator of binary length at most

    L=poly(e,B_K,D,g,H_F,H,h_c).                          (14)

There are O(eg) such coordinates, hence polynomial total output size.
An arbitrary field basis of arbitrarily large height can destroy a bound
stated using e alone; its presentation height must not be omitted.
Exact construction time additionally depends on the actual input
ideal/algebra's size and coefficient heights. A support-height existence
bound does not itself supply those input matrices for free.

For a reconstruction threshold, enlarge L so every rational coordinate
has numerator and denominator of absolute value <=2^L. If its residue
modulo an integer M is available and its denominator is coprime to M,
M>2^(2L+1) makes that coordinate unique by the cross-product bound for
two distinct fractions. Standard rational reconstruction then recovers
it in polynomial bit time. Certified real coordinate approximations
of error less than 2^(-2L-2) also isolate at most one such fraction.
These are conditional precision thresholds for correctly aligned
coordinates in the charged field presentation. They do not supply a
good prime, compatible field embeddings, the residues, a numerical lift,
or Galois descent from incompatible local data. A bad denominator prime
cannot simply be called good because its size is convenient.

## 7. Polynomial chart-exception count and use of support premises

Let the projective plane closure have degree D. The normalization's
pullback of a line has degree D. Therefore at most D geometric points
lie over the line at infinity. A nonzero polar of the defining homogeneous
equation has degree D-1, vanishes at all plane singular points, and can
be chosen to share no component with the reduced curve in characteristic
zero. Its pullback zero divisor has degree D(D-1). Every normalization
branch above a singular point contributes at least one. Consequently

    # {points outside the affine nonsingular plane locus} <= D^2. (15)

For D=1 there are no singular points. On the remaining locus the
normalization is an isomorphism, so the xy construction needs no extra
inverse-chart denominator. If a different supplied chart is used, its
additional denominator divisors must be charged: equations of degrees
k_i add at most D sum_i k_i preimages, unless a denominator vanishes
identically on a component and that chart is invalid there.

Thus the common-basepoint avoidance argument can charge A<=D^2 in
S_(N,A)=d+1+h_B+log(N(A+1)+1), in addition to whatever other exceptions
the chosen representation actually needs. This does not pay the degree
or coefficient height of a plane model that has not yet been produced.

If the preceding height theorem bounds only x=pi, there is a short
additional coordinate step when F is absolutely irreducible of positive
y-degree (or the x-map is nonconstant on every relevant component).
F(alpha,Y) is not the zero polynomial: otherwise x-alpha would be a
component. Specialization of the coefficient vector and the elementary
root-height bound give

    h(beta) <= H_F+D h(alpha)+C log(D+2).                 (16)

This remains true when the leading y-coefficient vanishes at alpha;
use the actual nonzero specialized polynomial. Summing with
multiplicities supplies (1) with

    H <= (D+1) sum_i m_i h(alpha_i)
         + g[H_F+C log(D+2)].                            (17)

No such deduction is valid on a vertical component with constant x.
In the intended finite-cover setting (17) transfers the established
pi-value bound to both plane coordinates once a polynomial-degree,
polynomial-height plane equation has been supplied.

## 8. Claim boundary and falsifiers

The accepted bridge is (2), the closed-algebra construction, and the
charged-field bit threshold (14). It includes arbitrary multiplicities
up to g, with explicit tangent denominators and interpolation denominators.
The strongest simple failures of a weaker statement are:

* Two branches over a plane singularity have identical x,y, so no c can
  give the asserted generator. Avoid those points as in (15).
* At a ramified support point, z-z_i need not generate the local maximal
  ideal; distinct support values alone do not encode a thickened divisor.
  The eta test is essential.
* Values x(P),y(P) without the curve equation do not determine jets.
  Equations (6)--(10), including H_F, are essential for the height claim.
* A degree-only number-field budget omits arbitrary basis conditioning;
  (13)--(14) require a charged field presentation.
* A height bound and an abstract divisor class do not provide a closed
  ideal, a canonical choice, an appropriate lift, or aligned local data.

No original-prime Frobenius identification, new native good-model theorem,
or unconditional reconstruction of unavailable torsion data follows here.
